reports.title: The Ceasefire That Isn't
reports.subtitle: Trump called Iran's peace proposal garbage. Iran called the US terms surrender. Brent crude hit $104. Nobody's blinking.

reports.title: Pump Relief as Political Triage
reports.subtitle: Gas hit $4.52. Trump wants to kill the gas tax. Congress needs to pass it. The Highway Trust Fund will pay.

reports.title: The Summit Without a Spine
reports.subtitle: Trump flies to Beijing Tuesday. Both sides want stability. Neither side can say what they actually need from the other.

reports.title: Three Days of Quiet, Then Drones on Kyiv
reports.subtitle: Trump's 72-hour Ukraine ceasefire expired at midnight. Russia struck residential buildings in Kyiv by 3:35 AM.

reports.title: The Chip Lab on National Television
reports.subtitle: Beijing showed Huawei's secret semiconductor research lab on prime-time TV three days before Trump lands. This was a message, not a documentary.

reports.title: OpenAI Buys Its Way Into Europe While Anthropic Waits
reports.subtitle: GPT-5.5-Cyber is now free to EU defenders. Anthropic's Mythos is not. This is not a cybersecurity story.

reports.title: Trump Names His Own Justices in Public, Warns the Birthright Ruling Will Follow
reports.subtitle: Gorsuch and Barrett voted wrong on tariffs. Now they face the birthright case. Trump is not asking for loyalty. He is documenting a grievance.

reports.title: The Inflation Number Lands Three Days Before the New Fed Chair Does
reports.subtitle: April CPI is expected at 3.8%, a 3-year high. Kevin Warsh takes over Friday. His first decision will be whether to pretend the last five years didn't happen.

reports.title: 184 Sanctioned Russian Ships Passed Through UK Waters. None Were Boarded.
reports.subtitle: Keir Starmer announced in March that British forces could now intercept shadow fleet tankers. Seven weeks later, the count is 238 journeys, zero boardings.

reports.title: Von der Leyen Wants to Delay Children's Access to Social Media. The Question Is Delay It Until When.
reports.subtitle: The EU is proposing a 'social media delay' for kids, backed by an age-verification app that is ready to deploy. Ten member states already have different rules.

reports.title: The Strike That Could Crack the Memory Market
reports.subtitle: Samsung's union wants 15% of operating profit. Management offered nothing. May 21 is the deadline. Micron stock is already up 6%.

reports.title: Colorado Rewrites Its AI Law. Congress Is About to Overwrite All of Them.
reports.subtitle: After two years and a lawsuit from Elon Musk, Colorado passed a weaker AI accountability law. A House Republican bill would nullify it before it takes effect.

reports.title: Trump Pulls 5,000 Troops from Germany. NATO's Eastern Flank Is Now Improvising.
reports.subtitle: Germany's 'Sparta 2.0' plan admits Europe cannot run a war without US software approval. Poland is competing for the troops like a trophy. The Baltics are watching both of them.

reports.title: The ICJ Said States Must Act on Climate. Now Vanuatu Is Trying to Make That Stick.
reports.subtitle: A 2025 court ruling said governments have a legal obligation to protect human rights from climate harm. Pacific island nations are pushing a UN resolution to turn it into accountability. The major emitters have not said yes.

reports.title: Fund ICE for Three Years. Also Build the Ballroom.
reports.subtitle: Senate Republicans returned from recess to pass a $72 billion immigration enforcement package. Trump wants $1 billion in the same bill for White House ballroom security. Vulnerable Republicans have to vote on both.
